full_judgment:
2. Facts stated in the writ-petition, in brief, are that the petitioner took loan from Janata Bank Limited (respondent number 2 herein), but failed to repay the same. As a result, the creditor-bank instituted Artha Rin Suit Number 41 of 2010 before the Artha Rin Adalat Number 1, Dhaka for an amount of Taka 3,32,80,955 and the suit was decreed ex-parte on 23-9-2010. As the petitioner failed to make payment of the decretal amount, the decree holder-bank filed Artha Jari Case Number 52 of 2011 and accordingly the said execution case was disposed of on 6-1-2014 issuing a certificate under section 33 (5) of the Ain, 2003. Thereafter, the decree holder-bank filed second execution case being Artha Jari Case Number 10 of 2015 on 26-1-2015 and filed an application for an order of civil imprisonment of the judgment debtor. The Executing Court allowed the application ex-parte, passed an order of civil imprisonment against the judgment debtor and by the same order issued warrant of arrest against him. In that event, the petitioner moved in this Court with the present application and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay 

 3. Mr Md Jamal Hossain, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the application for civil imprisonment of the petitioner was vague, unspecified and misleading. Earlier by order dated 20-2-2014 passed in the Artha Jari Case Number 52 of 2011, respondent number 2 got the right of possession, sale and enjoyment of the mortgaged property under section 33(5) of the Ain, but the decree holder-bank neither took any attempt to sell the said property in auction nor adjusted any amount as per Section 33(6Ka) of the Ain, and without adjustment of the value of the mortgaged property, filed the second execution case and obtained the impugned order in an illegal execution proceeding. The impugned order is, therefore, liable to be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 4. On the other hand, Mr Md Nazmul Hoque, learned advocate appearing for respondent number 2 (Janata Bank Limited) submits that the writ-petitioner did not take any steps for correction of the execution application, filed the writ petition challenging the order of civil imprisonment, which is not maintainable. He next submits that the decree holder-bank is ready to deduct the value of the mortgaged property in the execution case. 

 6. We have considered the submissions of the learned advocates of both the sides and gone through the record. It appears that Artha Jari Case Number 52 of 2011 was disposed of on 6-1-2014 issuing certificate of possession, enjoyment and sale of the mortgaged property in favour of the decree holder-bank under section 33(5) of the Ain. Admittedly, the second execution case being Artha Jari Case Number 10 of 2015 was filed by the decree holder-bank without adjustment of the value of the mortgaged property as required under section 33(6Ka) of the Ain, 2003. The decree holder-bank filed the second execution case in violation of the said provision of the Ain and obtained the order of civil imprisonment against the writ-petitioner, which appears to have been passed beyond the scope of law and, as such, without lawful authority. We, thus, find merit in the Rule to that extent. 

 Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned order is declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The decree holder-bank is, however, at liberty to make necessary amendment towards adjustment of the value of the mortgaged property according to the prevailing market price and file fresh application under section 34(1) of the Ain, 2003.
